title: Memorisation vs. in-context lookup (canonical vs. random order)
question: How do in-distribution sample efficiency and minimum required depth compare across a fixed canonical alphabet (`resample_alphabet=False`, where static weight memorisation is possible and the `B^L` problem universe overlaps between train and eval at small B, L), per-problem shuffled canonical glyphs (`symbol_pool_size=B, resample_alphabet=True`), and random 240-byte alphabets? (Zero-shot transfer to OOD permuted canonical alphabets after canonical exposure is tested in `addition/prior-override`.)
